title: Review lab notes and mini experiments: hotspots, rollback heuristics, and quick refactors
content:
Top-level intent:
- Quick, low-friction experiments and review notes for runtime refactors and rollback heuristics. Keep it messy and actionable.

Running thoughts / context:
- Working on a small delta to KV-cache eviction and the request batching sampler. Client repros show intermittent latency spikes at ~p95 when sequence length variance increases. Suspect warmup + rare cache thrash.
- Goal: have a small, reviewable PR (<200 LOC) with observability hooks so we can measure p50/p95 shifts and easily revert.

Checklist for PR prep (short):
- [ ] Annotate every change with one-line rationale in code comments (helps reviewers).
- [ ] Add a lightweight metric: kv_cache.evictions_by_reason (tagged).
- [ ] Unit test: eviction policy boundary conditions (min/max keys, aged entries).
- [ ] Integration smoke: run against microbench harness for 10k small requests + 1k long-tail requests.
- [ ] Docs: add short paragraph in serving-runtime/NOTES.md about risk and mitigation.
- [ ] Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback to previous variant if error_rate > 0.5% or p95 latency regresses by >15%.

Small experiment matrix (what to try quickly):
1) Conservative LRU bias: make the eviction threshold 1.5x current usage for 48h. Measure throughput and mem usage.
   - Hypothesis: reduces thrash, increases mem usage slightly.
   - Metric keys to track: kv_cache.size_bytes, kv_cache.evictions_by_reason, request.latency.p95
2) Batch sampler adjustment: when variance(seq_len) > X, reduce batch_max_tokens by 20% for new batches.
   - Hypothesis: reduces tail latency at cost of tokens/s. Good trade for latency-sensitive routes.
3) Opportunistic prefix cache: store common prefixes for top N customers for 1s only, then fall back.
   - Can be toggled per-route in config; low-risk to test.

Quick refactor ideas (tiny, low-risk):
- Extract the eviction reason enum into its own file and centralize the counter increments so tests can assert reasons deterministically.
- Rename sampler->batch_selector to reduce confusion in code comments (legacy naming).
- Inline a tiny helper used only by tests and runtime into a single test helper file to avoid accidental export.

Notes-to-self: Review comments I expect and how to pre-empt them
- "Why not just increase cache size?" -> add cost tradeoff notes and metric showing mem vs latency.
- "How tested on long tails?" -> include harness script in PR and attach output.
- "What happens on OOM?" -> document fallback behavior and assert no panic path.

Open questions / tradeoffs to write up in PR description:
- Is 15% p95 regression threshold too tight for short bursts? (could cause false rollbacks).
- Should the ephemeral prefix cache be per-instance or per-pool? Per-instance reduces cross-pool coherence but is simpler.
- How much observability retention do we need on these counters for debugging? 7 days vs 30 days tradeoff.

Follow-ups to schedule after merge (if green):
- Add a post-deploy smoke job that hits a curated prompt set for top 20 customers within 1 hour of rollout.
- Capture a few failing traces and add to the regression test suite as golden prompts.
- Small doc: "How to revert canary" with exact API commands and expected states.

Experiment log (quick snippets):
- 2024-11-09: Ran conservative LRU bias at 5% canary for 2 hours. p95 down 8%, mem up ~12%. No errors.
- 2024-11-12: Batch sampler tweak locally reduced p99 by ~20% on synthetic skewed seq lengths. Need longer run.

Slack / PR references to include in PR description:
- Slack thread: #runtime-kv -> thread ts 1700xxxxxx (link in GitHub PR).
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3842 (earlier attempt to add eviction metrics)
- Jira: RD-5123 for the overall kv cache reliability epic.

Tiny heuristics for reviewers (what I want feedback on):
- "Stop me if any change increases GC pressure noticeably."
- Prefer concrete test suggestions over vague "make safer" comments. If you see safety gaps, propose specific assertion/metric to add.

If I get stuck while writing PR:
- Pause and add a TODO comment in code referencing this doc and push a small WIP branch.
- Ping Rina for quick pairing on tests.

Misc ideas to try later (parking lot):
- Adaptive eviction threshold that learns from recent hit/miss ratio (non-blocking periodic adjuster).
- Route-scoped cache sizing: allocate small budgets per-route based on recent token-volume.

End note: keep the PR <200 LOC, prefer adding observability over algorithmic complexity for first iteration. Reverts should be trivial (one config flip + rollback).

-- mila
